answer.rationale: The write-path latency began climbing ~90 minutes ago, shortly after a release shipped 2 hours ago — temporal correlation makes a release regression the leading hypothesis. memory_b1 supports rollback as fast, stable, and customer-safe. Alternatives fit poorly: failover (b2) addresses regional faults, not a correlated-with-release regression; circuit breakers (b4) target partner dependency failures with no evidence of one here; read replicas (b5) offload reads, but the degradation is on the write path; adding capacity (b3) helps demand-driven surges but risks masking a code regression during peak settlement writes. Rollback is reversible, preserves in-flight writes (prior build was stable), and directly removes the most probable cause. Uncertainty remains: if latency persists post-rollback, capacity becomes the next-window action.
